evidence: Draft judged: "You want to be able to let the quiet little preferences that you have bubble up to the surface and know for sure that you’re not going by what your social group would want you to do." It sits once, verbatim, as the last sentence of the "Temporary Separation" paragraph in CONTEXT.txt, with no quote marks round "social", as the_change says. Compared word by word with SOURCE.txt: his published guide ("Sometimes a temporary, intentional period of distance from the people or group supplying the answers helps quieter preferences surface. Use that distance only long enough to tell your own signal from the social echo.") and the replaced words ("You want to let your quieter preferences bubble up to the surface so you can be sure you’re not just echoing your social group."). It does what the_change says: Emulate's sentence as it came, and the_change names no fix besides the quote marks. Kept: the aim of letting his quieter preferences surface ("bubble up to the surface" is the replaced sentence's own image), the aim of being sure they are the reader's own and not the group's, and the group as the people the earlier sentence says the reader gets answers from. No number, person, source or fact is added. Differences I checked and accept as paraphrase, not new claims: (1) "echoing your social group" (his "social echo") becomes "going by what your social group would want you to do": the group's imagined wishes for your actions in place of its views echoed back. That tilts from echo toward compliance and drops the word "echo" from the paragraph (the section heading, "your voice is everybody else's voice", still carries the idea). I accept it because it is the same internalised pull of the group: the guide itself frames the problem this way ("You don't know what you want, until you have heard what someone else wants"; "neither in rebellion nor in compliance with others"), and his "the people or group supplying the answers" already gives the group an active part. This is the largest drift, and he may want to see that "echoing" became "going by what the group would want". (2) "so you can be sure" becomes "and know for sure": the two aims now sit side by side instead of the first serving the second; his published pair is also two aims in sequence, and the sentence still says the reader wants both. (3) "not just echoing" becomes "not going by", and "just" is gone, so it reads a shade more absolute; "for sure" is as strong as the replaced "be sure", and "going by" (using something as a guide) still allows an overlap with the group's wishes. (4) "your quieter preferences" becomes "the quiet little preferences that you have": the comparative goes and a warm "little" comes in, which is tone and not a claim; "that you have" repeats "your". (5) "be able to let" for "let" adds an ability, not a condition. His published "only long enough" is absent here and in the replaced words, and the change does not say it puts it back. Linter D9 (follows the source order): accepted. One sentence replaces one, in the order of the published guide (preferences surface, then telling the signal from the echo), and the sentence notices something inside it (that the pull is the group's imagined wishes, not only its voice), so T13 and T09 do not apply. Linter E36/E41 heavy second person (13.5 'you' per 100 of my words): accepted. The count is 5 second-person words in 37, and the sentence it replaces had 5 in 24 (about 21 per 100), so the draft is lighter than what it replaces, although a little denser than the paragraph's other sentences; the whole section speaks to "you" ("You are in the first camp if:", "you can ask yourself:"), and this sentence gives the purpose of the separation, which is a reason and not coaching alone. Tell rows T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 were judged on the literal draft in its context and none is PRESENT. Looked at closely: T22 (it opens with the coach pattern "You want to be able to", but it carries the reason for the separation that the paragraph has not yet given, so it is not reassurance with no reason); T06 (the image and "preferences" are the replaced sentence's own and come from his published "surface" and "preferences"); T15 (a recast in a different voice, not rarer words swapped in, and the whole change is Emulate's rewrite, as the brief says); T21 (two aims in one sentence, simply joined); T29 (the last sentence adds the purpose of the separation, so cutting it would lose a consideration); T20 and T28 (a plain ending, not a polished closer or uplift); C02 ("that you have" points at the preferences). Provenance note on ADMISSION.json, not on the draft: its T14 and T15 evidence says the sentence "puts back the author's own point that Emulate dropped", which is boilerplate here because the_change says nothing was put back; the ABSENT statuses still stand.
